routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Citizens of visa-exempt countries can visit for up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. Use the official questionnaire to check your passport.

other: Which nationalities are visa-exempt is shown by the official visa questionnaire, not a fixed list on these pages.
Check entry conditions and ETIAS on official EU pages; the Dutch pages read did not cover them.

sources.label: Netherlands Worldwide: how long can I visit

routes.name: Short-stay Schengen visa (type C)
routes.summary: For travelers who need a visa for up to 90 days in 180 days. You normally apply in the country where you live, between 6 months and 15 days before travel.

other: Applies to nationalities that are not visa-exempt.
Fee, processing time and document checklists vary by embassy and were not confirmed here. See the checklists on netherlandsworldwide.nl.

steps: Check if you need a visa with the official questionnaire.
Apply at the Dutch embassy or consulate (or its service partner) in your country of residence.
Apply between 6 months and 15 days before you travel.

routes.name: Airport transit visa (type A)
routes.summary: Needed by some nationalities for a stop or plane change at a Dutch airport. It does not let you pass passport control or visit the Netherlands.

other: Which nationalities need it was not listed on the pages read. Use the official visa questionnaire.

routes.name: MVV (provisional residence permit)
routes.summary: A long-stay entry sticker many people need to travel to the Netherlands and collect their residence permit. Your sponsor or you apply together with the residence permit, then collect the MVV at a Dutch embassy.

other: Some nationalities are exempt. See the IND MVV exemptions page.

stay.note: Collect the MVV within 3 months of approval, then travel within the 90-day MVV validity.

steps: Apply for the MVV and residence permit together.
If approved, book an appointment at the Dutch embassy or consulate to get the sticker.
Travel to the Netherlands and collect your residence permit at the IND.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss free movement
routes.summary: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can live and work in the Netherlands without a permit. After 3 months you need to be working, have enough income, or be a student with health insurance.

other: Longer than 3 months: economically active (earn at least 50% of the social assistance amount or work at least 40% of a full week), enough income, or enrolled student with insurance and enough funds.
Register at your town hall (BRP) if staying longer than 4 months. Get health insurance within 4 months.

stay.note: Permanent right of residence after 5 years of qualifying residence.

sources.label: IND: staying as an EU, EEA or Swiss citizen
Netherlands Worldwide: visit up to 3 months

routes.name: Highly skilled migrant (kennismigrant) residence permit
routes.summary: Work permit for skilled hires by an IND-recognized sponsor. Salary must meet a yearly threshold. No separate work permit needed.

income.note: Gross per month without holiday pay, age 30 or older, 2026. Under 30: EUR 4,357. Reduced criterion (orientation year or within 3 years of graduation): EUR 3,122.

other: Employer must be a recognized sponsor on the IND public register.
Employer applies for you.

stay.note: Valid for the length of your contract, up to 5 years. If you lose your job you get 3 months to find a new one (6 months in some cases from 22 May 2026).

steps: Find a recognized sponsor to hire you.
Sponsor submits the application (and the MVV if needed).
Collect the MVV sticker if required, travel, and collect your permit.

routes.name: EU Blue Card (Netherlands)
routes.summary: Work permit for degree holders or experienced professionals with a job offer of at least 6 months and a high salary. Valid up to 5 years.

income.note: Gross per month without holiday pay, 2026. Reduced criterion: EUR 4,754.

eligibility.education: Higher education degree of at least 3 years, or 5 years of relevant experience (3 years within the last 7 for IT roles)
other: Employment contract valid for at least 6 months.
Employer applies for you.
Regulated and BIG-registered professions have extra requirements.

stay.note: Stays valid until 3 months after the contract ends. 3 months to find new work after unemployment (6 months after 2 years on the permit).

routes.processing: IND page gives no processing time.

routes.name: Intra-corporate transferee permit (ICT)
routes.summary: For managers, specialists and trainees from a non-EU company being transferred to its Dutch branch. You must have worked for the company outside the EU for at least 3 months.

other: Salary must meet the highly skilled migrant salary criterion (see the IND required amounts page).
Valid for up to 3 years for managers and specialists, 1 year for trainees.

stay.note: Trainees up to 1 year. EU-wide cap of 3 years.

routes.name: Seasonal work permit
routes.summary: For seasonal work in agriculture or horticulture for a Dutch employer, up to 24 weeks. The employer must first look for workers in the Netherlands and EU and provide housing.

other: Must meet income requirements and pay the standard collective agreement wage.
Not stayed in the Netherlands illegally in the last 3 years.

routes.name: Self-employed person residence permit
routes.summary: For freelancers and business owners whose work is of essential interest to the Dutch economy. The RVO scores you on personal experience, business plan and added value.

other: Pass the points test: at least 30 points in each of the three areas, or 45 each for experience and business plan.
KvK (Chamber of Commerce) registration and any needed permits.
Freelancers need one or more commissions in the Netherlands.
Must meet income requirements, shown in your business plan. See the IND required amounts page.

stay.note: Valid up to 2 years. After 5 years of work you no longer need a work permit.

routes.name: Dutch-American Friendship Treaty (DAFT) permit
routes.summary: Self-employed permit for US citizens (Dutch-Japanese treaty for Japanese). No points test. You usually invest at least EUR 4,500 in your business.

investment.note: Generally required for most business forms. Detailed rules are only in Dutch.

other: One of: trade between NL and the US or Japan, lead operations as a key representative of a US or Japanese business, practice an independent profession (not government or healthcare), or invest substantial capital.
First application: register with KvK and make the investment within 6 months of the decision letter or the IND may revoke the permit.
Extensions need annual accounts plus a balance sheet or income statement.

routes.name: Start-up residence permit
routes.summary: One-year permit for founders of an innovative start-up backed by an approved facilitator (mentor). It cannot be extended as a start-up.

other: Written contract with a facilitator on the RVO list.
Product, technology or way of working must be new to the Netherlands.
Funds must cover your whole stay of up to 1 year, plus a step-by-step plan.

stay.note: After 1 year apply for the self-employed permit, with a facilitator declaration of at least 3 months of mentoring.

routes.processing: IND decision should come within 90 days.

routes.name: Orientation year permit (graduates and researchers)
routes.summary: One year to look for work or start a business after finishing a Dutch degree, a degree at a top-ranked foreign university, or research in the Netherlands.

eligibility.education: Dutch bachelor's or master's, post-master's of 10+ months, master's/PhD at a top-200 foreign university, Erasmus Mundus master's, or Dutch research permit, within the last 3 years
other: Foreign institution must be top 200 in at least 2 of the THE, QS and ShanghaiRanking lists on your graduation date.
Foreign graduates need IELTS 6.0 or equivalent, or a program taught in English or Dutch.
Foreign diplomas need a Nuffic evaluation.

routes.name: Study residence permit (university or HBO)
routes.summary: For full-time study at a recognized Dutch institution, which applies on your behalf. You can work up to 16 hours a week or full time in June to August with an employer work permit.

income.note: 2026 amount for HBO and university students per the IND.

other: Institution must be an IND recognized sponsor.
Full-time study and Dutch health insurance.
Study progress of at least half the credits per year.
Permit length is the course plus 3 months, up to 5 years.
Some nationalities need an MVV and some are exempt. Check the IND list.
Working rules and sufficient-means details come from an IND brochure of unclear date, so confirm before applying.

stay.note: Course length plus 3 months, up to 5 years.

routes.name: Working holiday permit
routes.summary: One-year cultural exchange permit for young people from partner countries. Quotas apply: 100 per year for Argentina, Uruguay, Hong Kong and Taiwan, 200 for Japan and South Korea.

other: Never held a regular Dutch residence permit before.
Return ticket or money to buy one, enough money for your stay, and health insurance.
Must live in your country of nationality when applying, per your country's agreement.

routes.name: Residence permit for partner
routes.summary: For a foreign spouse or partner of a Dutch citizen or permit holder. Many partners must pass the civic integration exam abroad and get an MVV first.

income.note: Gross, without holiday pay, 1 July to 31 December 2026 for a sponsor with a partner.

other: Sponsor must be Dutch or hold a valid residence permit that allows family.
Basic civic integration exam passed abroad, unless exempt.
Minimum age is 18 for existing marriages and 21 for new ones or unmarried partners, per an IND brochure of unclear date. Confirm on ind.nl.
Sponsors who must integrate need 1 year of residence first, with exceptions.

stay.note: 5 years if sponsor is Dutch or permanent. Otherwise ends with the sponsor's permit.

routes.name: Residence permit for minor child, adopted, foster or Dutch child (Chavez)
routes.summary: For a child under 18 joining a parent in the Netherlands, an adopted or foster child, or a non-EU parent living with a minor Dutch child. Check the IND pages for each case.

other: The IND lists separate permits for minor child, child born in NL, adopted child, foster child, and a minor Dutch child (Chavez).
Parents of adults and other relatives: only via Article 8 ECHR family life, case by case. Parents were not mentioned in the IND brochure.

routes.name: Permanent residence permit (EU long-term resident)
routes.summary: After 5 consecutive years on a valid permit you can apply. You must pass the civic integration exam at level A2 and have independent, sustainable income.

income.note: Own income, gross without holiday pay, 1 July to 31 December 2026. Family member who is married or cohabiting: EUR 2,337.

eligibility.language: Civic integration exam at A2 (or exempt)
other: Main residence in the Netherlands throughout. Only years from age 8 count.
Blue Card holders can sometimes apply sooner. Other exceptions exist, see the IND page.

stay.note: No end date. The residence document is renewed every 5 years.

routes.name: Naturalization (Dutch citizenship)
routes.summary: After 5 consecutive years on a valid residence permit and passing the civic integration exam at A2. The decision period is 12 months, then you attend a ceremony within a year.

eligibility.language: Civic integration exam at A2 (or exempt)
other: Apply at your municipality.
Shorter terms exist: 3 years with a Dutch partner you lived with for 3 years, or after 2 years if you lived in the Kingdom 10 years in total.

citizenship.note: You must usually give up your other nationality. Exceptions: marriage or partnership with a Dutch citizen at the time of the Royal Decree, recognized refugees, born in the Kingdom and living there, automatic loss or impossible renunciation in the home country, unrecognized states, or serious consequences from renouncing.

routes.name: Naturalization for partners of Dutch citizens (3 years)
routes.summary: Cut to 3 years of continuous residence if you lived with the same Dutch partner for 3 years. Your partner must be Dutch when you apply. Same A2 integration requirement.

eligibility.language: Civic integration exam at A2 (or exempt)
other: Valid permit or EU residency throughout the 3 years.
Married, registered or unmarried partners count.

citizenship.note: Renunciation rules are the same as for naturalization. The renunciation exemption for marriage only covers those already married or partnered at the date of the Royal Decree.

routes.name: Dutch citizenship by birth or descent, and option
routes.summary: You are Dutch at birth if one or both parents are Dutch. A short option procedure (about 3 months) exists for a legally defined group. Generation limits were not on the pages read.

other: Descent rules beyond a Dutch parent, and who qualifies for option, were not detailed on the pages read. Check the IND option page.

citizenship.note: Option usually does not require giving up your other nationality.

fees.label: Option, child under 18 with a parent

routes.name: Asylum
routes.summary: Applying for asylum is free. You get an asylum residence permit if you need protection. See the IND for the procedure, which changed for applications from 12 June 2026.

other: Permanent asylum residency applications are no longer possible from 12 June 2026.
